problem_statement: A caller who inserts an item into a singly-linked list that is already present in that same list should have the existing occurrence moved to the new position, not duplicated. Observably, re-inserting (or re-adding) an element that already appears in the list leaves the element in its old spot and adds a second occurrence, so the list grows by one and reports an inflated length, and the head/tail links no longer match what the caller built. For example, after a list has four items, re-adding one of those four items must leave the list at four items with the re-added item in its new slot; instead the list reports five items and the tail is wrong. The required behavior is that inserting an item that is already in the list moves it to the new position while keeping the list's length and head/tail linkage consistent, and that inserting a brand-new item still appends or inserts it normally.

superseded_statements.problem_statement: list_insert must remove the newitem from the list before re-inserting it; when an already-present element is re-inserted, the old implementation corrupts the linkage and the list length.
check_issues: `problem_statement` gives the fix away: "list_insert must remove the newitem from the list before re-inserting it;"; "when an already-present element is re-inserted, the old implementation corrupts the linkage and the list length.". Describe only the observable symptom, its trigger and the required behavior, not what the code checks or must do internally

causal_chain: The upstream unit test 'Singly-linked list' (test_list) builds a list, then re-adds element 2 with list_add and re-inserts element 3 with list_insert, asserting that the list length stays 4 and that the tail and links are correct. Before the fix, re-inserting an item that already exists in the list does not first detach its old occurrence, so the element appears twice and the length/ tail assertions fail. After the fix, re-inserting detaches the existing occurrence first, so the item moves to its new position, the length remains 4, and the head/tail and next-link assertions pass.
